newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Italy late to enact rules on plants and animals.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Italy late to enact rules on plants and animals.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found Italy was late in enacting Community rules governing plant propogation and bovine embryo health conditions.

The Commission initiated action in the court after Italy failed to notify when and how it would transpose Council directives on fruit and ornamental plant proprogating, potato ring rot control and animal health conditions on bovine embryo trade in and out of the Community.
Italy did not deny allegations that it had not fulfilled its obligations, but told the court the national authorities encountered procedural and legal problems.
The Commission dropped its action regarding the potato ring rot rules as Italy adopted the directive on 27 February 1996.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Italian)
"Failure to fulfil obligations - Failure to transpose directives 93/48/EEC, 93/49/EEC, 93/52/EEC, 93/61/EEC and 93/85/EEC"
Commission of the European Communities, applicant

application for a declaration that by not adopting and bringing into force within the prescribed periods the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with directives 93/48/EEC, 93/49/EEC, 93/52/EEC, 93/61/EEC and 93/85/EEC, the Italian Republic has failed to fulfil its obligations under those directives and under the EC Treaty

1. Declares that, by not adopting and bringing into force within the prescribed periods the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with directives 93/48/EEC, 93/49/EEC, 93/52/EEC, 93/61/EEC, the Italian Republic has failed to fulfil its obligations under article 10 of directive 93/48, article 8 of directive 93/49, article 2 of 93/52 and article 7 of directive 93/61
2. Orders the Italian Republic to pay the costs.
